land.text: the Sivas-Tokat-Niksar-Amasya plateau of central Anatolia, where the Danishmends 'established themselves' after Manzikert (1071)

predecessors.note: The page names no holder; the Byzantine Empire is the neighbour Cliopatria lists from 1094 and the power Manzikert broke.

land.text: the same plateau, which Cliopatria still draws inside the Great Seljuk shape of 1085-1093

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Great Seljuk shape of 1085-1093 covers the Danishmend lands (99% of the 1094 shape); the pages show a separate Danishmend emirate.

land.text: the Danishmend remnant: Sivas (1174), Malatya (1178) and the rest of 'the Danishmend lands' taken by Kilij Arslan II

successors.note: The Sultanate of Rum page: Kilij Arslan II 'captured the remaining territories around Sivas and Malatya from the last of the Danishmends'. Cliopatria carries the Danishmend row to 1187; the Danishmendids page ends the dynasty in 1178.

capitals.name: Niksar (Neocaesarea)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Sivas Niksar' without years; 'The capital was likely first established in Amasia' (no year). The years are my assumption (confidence 1); coordinates approximate, the gazetteer has no Niksar.

capitals.name: Sivas
capitals.note: Yağıbasan, 'based in Sivas' (Yağıbasan page), minted coins there in 1142-1164; Mesud I held it in 1150-1155 and Rum absorbed the Sivas lands in 1174.

capitals.name: Malatya (Melitene)
capitals.note: Last seat: 'In 1178, Malatya was occupied. This event marked the end of the Danishmend rule.' Nasreddin Muhammed ruled from 1175 as a Seljuk vassal; his seat is not named on the page (confidence 1).

correction.text: the Danishmend emirate of central Anatolia, outline of 1094 carried back to 1075

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1075-1093: the infobox gives 'Established: 1071/1075' and the page 'The Danishmends established themselves in Anatolia in the aftermath of the Battle of Manzikert in 1071', but Cliopatria's row starts in 1094. No page gives the extent before 1094; the 1094 outline is carried back unchanged (confidence 1). Cliopatria's Great Seljuk shape covers the same land in 1085-1093.

58,622 km2 for 1094-1098: the Niksar-Tokat-Sivas-Amasya core (Sivas 73%, Tokat 100%, Ordu 91%), which fits the infobox capitals Sivas and Niksar. The infobox gives no area; the exact outline is unverified: page budget. In 1100 Emir Gazi captured Bohemond of Antioch.

correction.text: the 1099 shape without Malatya, which the Danishmends take in September 1101

keyframe_review.note: 71,024 km2 for 1099-1110: the shape adds Kayseri (52%) and Malatya (27%) from 1099. The Malatya page has Gabriel of Melitene keep his independence 'From 1086 to 1100 ... with the aid of the Beylik of the Danishmends' and the Danishmends take the city 'one year later in 1101 following the Battle of Melitene' (a footnote: 'In September 1101, the Danishmend Turks captured Malatya'); the Danishmendids page says 1103. Malatya is taken out for 1099-1100 and put back by the 1101 keyframe. Kayseri is unverified: the pages show it Danishmend only by 1146.

New keyframe, 1101-1110: Malatya joins ('In September 1101, the Danishmend Turks captured Malatya'; the Danishmendids page says 'which they captured in 1103', the Bohemond captivity ending the same year). The outline is Cliopatria's 1099 shape, Kayseri unverified.

77,491 km2 for 1111-1138 (Malatya 55%). Consistent with a Danishmend state that helped Mesud I take Konya in 1116, killed Bohemond II in battle in 1130 and held the title Melik from the caliph in 1134. Outline otherwise unverified: page budget.

77,465 km2 for 1139-1151, the same outline. 'When Mehmed died in 1142, the Danishmend lands were divided between his two brothers' (Yağıbasan at Sivas, Ayn al-Dawla at Malatya); Emir Gazi died at Kayseri in 1146 and Yağıbasan deposed his elder son Zinnun there; in 1150 Mesud I captured Sivas and Yağıbasan became a Seljuk vassal. The shape keeps the whole dynasty as one state; the divisions are not drawn.

85,779 km2 for 1152-1168: Kayseri now 87% and Kahramanmaras (Elbistan) 23%. Right in kind: Yağıbasan held Sivas, Tokat, Niksar and Kayseri (after deposing Zinnun in 1146) and 'later captured Elbistan from the Seljuks' with Byzantine help after the defeat at Aksaray in 1155 (undated), so the Elbistan part is early by a few years; the Malatya branch is not on the Yağıbasan page. Infobox gives no area.

85,805 km2 for 1169-1176: right for 1169-1173 only. 'when Nur ad-Din died in 1174, the Sivas lands were incorporated into the Sultanate' and the Kilij Arslan II page has him refuse in 1175 'to hand over to Manuel the territory conquered from the Danishmends'; the shape from 1174 is the remnant (new keyframe 1174). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1169..1173 from this entry's own 'valid 1169-1173 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the Danishmend remnant after the loss of the Sivas lands (Cliopatria's 1177 outline used from 1174)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1174-1176: the Sivas lands go to the Sultanate in 1174 and 'By 1175 Nasreddin Muhammed had returned to power, and ruled as a Seljuk vassal'. The page does not list what he held; Cliopatria's 1177 remnant (41,685 km2: Kayseri, Malatya, Elbistan, part of Sivas) is used from 1174 (confidence 1 for the exact outline).

41,685 km2 for 1177-1187: right for 1177-1178 only. 'In 1178, Malatya was occupied. This event marked the end of the Danishmend rule'; the Sultanate of Rum page has Kilij Arslan II capture 'the remaining territories around Sivas and Malatya from the last of the Danishmends'. The Malatya page says the Seljuks held Malatya fully only from 1177. Years 1179-1187 must not be drawn as Danishmend; they belong to the Sultanate of Rum. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1177..1178 from this entry's own 'valid 1177-1178 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: central Anatolia around Niksar, Tokat, Sivas and Amasya

ledger.note: 1075: the Danishmend emirate arises in central Anatolia. Infobox 'Established: 1071/1075' and 'The Danishmends established themselves in Anatolia in the aftermath of the Battle of Manzikert in 1071'; ruler list '1071/1075-1084: Danishmend Gazi'; 'The capital was likely first established in Amasia'. The page's own account of the rise is uneven (it also has Gazi act on the death of Suleyman I of Rum in 1086). The page names no former holder.

1101: the Danishmends take Malatya. 'The Danishmends took Malatya one year later in 1101 following the Battle of Melitene' (footnote: 'In September 1101, the Danishmend Turks captured Malatya'); Gabriel of Melitene had kept the city independent in 1086-1100 with Danishmend help. The Danishmendids page puts the capture in 1103.

ledger.counterpart: Zinnun (Dhu'l-Nun), Emir Gazi's elder son at Kayseri
ledger.note: 1146: Yağıbasan takes Kayseri. Emir Gazi died in Kayseri in 1146; his elder son Zinnun succeeded him there 'but Yağıbasan, based in Sivas, deposed him', uniting Sivas and Kayseri (a quarrel inside the dynasty). [Reviewer me-09-a, 2026-10-25: confidence 3 -> 2: the Yağıbasan page dates Emir Gazi's death at Kayseri to 1146 but gives no year for the deposition of Zinnun.]

1150: Mesud I captures Sivas. 'After Seljuk Sultan Mesut I captured Sivas, Yağıbasan became a Seljuk vassal' (Yağıbasan page). The page does not say Sivas was given back; Cliopatria keeps Sivas Danishmend to 1173 and the Danishmendids page has the Sivas lands incorporated only in 1174. [Reviewer me-09-a, 2026-10-25: confidence 3 -> 2: the Yağıbasan page dates Yağıbasan's submission ('in 1150 Yağıbasan agreed to be a vassal of the Seljuks'), not Mesud I's capture of Sivas.]

1155: Yağıbasan fails against Kilij Arslan II. Mesud died in 1155; Yağıbasan, 'allied with other Danishmend rulers', attacked Kilij Arslan II 'but was defeated at Aksaray'. With Byzantine help he later captured Elbistan from the Seljuks (undated, ledger below).

1155: Yağıbasan captures Elbistan. The page says only that 'With Byzantine help, he later captured Elbistan from the Seljuks' after the 1155 defeat at Aksaray; the year is my placement at the page's last dated event (confidence 1). Cliopatria's 1152 shape already holds Kahramanmaras.

region.text: the Sivas lands: Sivas, Tokat, Amasya

ledger.note: 1174: the Sivas lands pass to the Sultanate. 'when Nur ad-Din died in 1174, the Sivas lands were incorporated into the Sultanate' (Sultanate of Rum page: Kilij Arslan II 'captured the remaining territories around Sivas and Malatya'); in 1175 he refused to give Manuel 'the territory conquered from the Danishmends' (Kilij Arslan II page). Tokat and Amasya are in the region as my reading: the page says only 'the Sivas lands', the Cliopatria remnant lacks them.

region.text: Malatya and the remaining Danishmend lands

ledger.note: 1178: Malatya is occupied and Danishmend rule ends. 'In 1178, Malatya was occupied. This event marked the end of the Danishmend rule.' The occupier is not named on the Danishmendids page; the Sultanate of Rum page has Kilij Arslan II take 'the remaining territories around Sivas and Malatya from the last of the Danishmends'; the Malatya page says the Seljuks held the city fully from 1177.

region.text: the last Danishmend lands, now the Sultanate of Rum's

ledger.note: 1178: the Danishmend dynasty ends. The infobox gives 'Disestablished: 1178'; 'By 1175 Nasreddin Muhammed had returned to power, and ruled as a Seljuk vassal.' Cliopatria draws the row to 1187.

wars.name: Danishmend capture of Bohemond of Antioch
wars.outcome: Emir Gazi captured Bohemond I of Antioch in 1100 and held him until 1103; no border moved.
wars.note: The Battle of Melitene (1100) article could not be opened (url_not_found); the Danishmendids page gives the capture without a place.

wars.name: Crusade of 1101
wars.outcome: A Seljuk-Danishmend alliance defeated the Crusade of 1101 (Kilij Arslan I 'defeated three Crusade contingents'); the Danishmends take Malatya in September 1101.
wars.note: The Danishmendids page gives no year for the alliance; the Sultanate of Rum page dates the crusade defeat to 1101.

wars.name: Danishmend-Antioch war of 1130
wars.outcome: Bohemond II of Antioch was killed in battle with Emir Gazi in 1130; no border moved.

wars.name: Danishmend-Rum wars
wars.outcome: Mesud I takes Sivas (1150) and Yağıbasan becomes a vassal; Yağıbasan is beaten at Aksaray by Kilij Arslan II (1155) but takes Elbistan with Byzantine help; the Sultanate absorbs the Sivas lands (1174), Nasreddin Muhammed is a Seljuk vassal (1175) and Malatya is occupied in 1178.
wars.note: Sources for the steps: Yağıbasan page (1150, 1155), Danishmendids page (1174, 1175, 1178), Malatya page (Seljuk full control 1177), Kilij Arslan II page (1175 Manuel demand).

certainty.note: The Danishmend emirates of Niksar, Sivas, Kayseri and Malatya shared and exchanged land (1142 division, 1146 deposition of Zinnun); no frontier with Rum, Byzantium or the Crusader states is fixed on any page opened.

sources.title: Malatya
sources.note: Malatya: Gabriel 1086-1100, September 1101 capture, Danishmend hold to 1152, Seljuk full control 1177.

sources.title: Sultanate of Rum
sources.note: Kilij Arslan II captured the remaining territories around Sivas and Malatya; Mesud I and the Danishmends take Konya 1116; Crusade of 1101.

sources.title: Kilij Arslan II
sources.note: 1175 Manuel's demand for the territory conquered from the Danishmends; 1176 Myriokephalon (thin on the Danishmends).

notes: Pages: Danishmendids, Yağıbasan, Malatya, Sultanate of Rum and Kilij Arslan II (budget 5). Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Melitene_(1100) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaghi-Basan (url_not_found; the Yağıbasan article is at %C4%9F). The Kilij Arslan II and Sultanate of Rum pages are thin on the Danishmends (they have no Yağıbasan, Nur ad-Din or 1174 division). Cliopatria rows to correct: the row starts in 1094 although the dynasty is dated 1071/1075; 1099-1100 hold Malatya two years before the capture (September 1101 on the Malatya page, 1103 on the Danishmendids page); 1169-1176 keep the Sivas lands that the Sultanate absorbed in 1174; the 1177 shape runs to 1187 although the dynasty ended in 1178. NOT corrected though doubtful: Kayseri in 1099-1145 (the pages show it Danishmend only by 1146), the Danishmend lands of 1139-1151 as one state (Mehmed's lands were divided between brothers in 1142: Sivas, Malatya and Kayseri-Elbistan lines; the Danishmendids page lists separate rulers) and the 1177 remnant (the page does not say which lands Nasreddin Muhammed held). Not coded: Yağıbasan's Byzantine vassalage (a Greek seal c. 1146-1150: 'emir and servant of the emperor', Yağıbasan page) and Danishmend help to Mesud I at Konya in 1116 (the Sultanate of Rum page). Page disagreements: Malatya 1101 (Malatya page) against 1103 (Danishmendids page); Danishmend start 1071/1075 (infobox) against Gazi acting on Suleyman's death in 1086 (text); Seljuk full control of Malatya 1177 (Malatya page) against 1178 occupation (Danishmendids page); Danishmend hold of Malatya 'until 1152' (Malatya page). Native names are from general knowledge. Counterparts: the Kerman-like local lords are absent; the Armenian governor Gabriel of Melitene is named in the 1101 gain and has no dossier.
